why: B: for every abstract Riemannian ℝⁿ-manifold M isometric to Sⁿ via ψ (n > 2), q ≠ p, p': INTEGRAL singular homology of Ω(M; p, q) (blind Om) and of Ω* is ℤ in degrees k(n−1) and zero otherwise, and both are non-zero in infinitely many degrees. A (bettiNumber_sphere_paths; 𝕜 : Type, no universe parameters): for the embedded Sⁿ ⊆ ℝⁿ⁺¹, n ≥ 3, q ≠ ±p, over every field 𝕜, dim_𝕜 H_i(PathSp; 𝕜) = 1 if n−1 ∣ i else 0; Ω only. B ⇒ A needs the universal coefficient theorem (absent from Mathlib/project), plus transport from abstract M. A ⇒ B fails genuinely: besides the UCT, field Betti numbers do not determine integral homology without finite generation (⟨1/p : p prime⟩ ⊆ ℚ is torsion-free of dimension 1 over every field but not ≅ ℤ); the project computes homology from the energy filtration over fields and explicitly does not formalize the integral statement. Setting differences (abstract M via ψ; Ω* in B) are bridged on the embedded sphere, see below.
overlap: No A_to_B/B_to_A. For A_to_A_emb (#rt_check OK): 529 shared project theorems — slice-chart / riemDist / path-metric infrastructure of the Ω dictionary and the sphere's slice structure, the Appendix telescope machinery via theorem_17_1; bettiNumber_sphere_paths itself is used only through the hypothesis.
